newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary Danubius says releasing loan for takeover.
newsitem.headline: Hungary Danubius says releasing loan for takeover.

text.p: Danubius Hotels said on Wednesday that following the Competition Agency's approval of its takeover of the hotel chain Hungaria Szalloda Rt, it would immediately activate a bridging loan to pay for the deal.

"Everything is organised but within a couple of days we shall fix dates," Danubius' President and CEO Sandor Betegh told Reuters, adding that he had not yet been informed by the Competition Agency of its decision.
Hungary's Competition Agency said on Wednesday it had approved the 8.125 billion forint sale of hotel chain Hungaria Szalloda Rt to Danubius.

The state privatisation agency APV Rt approved the deal in August on condition that the Competition Agency established that the total market share of the merged hotel chains did not exceed the maximum permitted 30 percent.

Betegh said the company would be using three banks -- K&H, Creditinstalt and the Magyar Kulkereskedelmi Bank -- to secure a bridging loan covering 80 percent of the purchase price of 8.125 billion forints.
They will pay the remaining 20 percent with compensation coupons, which were issued by the last government to victims of fascism and communism and are freely traded on the Budapest Stock Exchange.

The price paid for the stake represents 173.8 percent of the face value of the shares and the remaining 15 percent stake will be offered to employees with Danubius obliged to buy any shares not subscribed also at 173.8 percent of face value.
Betegh said this would happen in the first half of next year.
"It will happen only next spring because there are various deadlines for offering the shares to employees," he said.
He said that all other conditions of the contract, including a stipulation that the new owner must refurbish the hotel chain at a cost of two billion forints over three years, will be fulfilled.

Other commitments include keeping on the entire 3,000-strong staff of Hungaria for at least two years and the public offering and introduction of at least 50 percent of Hungaria shares on the Budapest Stock Exchange within a year.

Doubts over whether the Competition Agency would approve the deal arose over the fact that combined market share of Danubius and Hungaria is around 27 percent in all categories of hotel but rises to above 30 percent if the Beta Hotel chain in which Danubius has shares is included.
However sources within Danubius said at the time of the sale that as the company does not actually control or manage Beta it would be left out of the equation.
Hungaria Szalloda, which as HungarHotels was the subject of a failed bid by American General Hospitality Corp of Dallas, Texas, early last year, is made up of 14 mainly provincial hotels.

Following the failed sale, the Budapest Forum was hived off for a separate sell-off, the tender for which was won by Intercontinental Hotels, who will pay $49.4 million, or 190 percent of face value, for a 94.91 percent stake.
